# Networking and Telecom Equipment — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global networking and telecom equipment vendors across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Cisco Systems | NASDAQ: CSCO |
| 2 | Huawei Technologies | Private (Shenzhen) |
| 3 | Nokia | NYSE: NOK |
| 4 | Ericsson | NASDAQ: ERIC |
| 5 | Arista Networks | NYSE: ANET |
| 6 | ZTE Corporation | HKEX: 0763 / SZSE: 000063 |
| 7 | NEC Corporation | TYO: 6701 |
| 8 | Samsung Networks (Samsung Electronics Networks Business) | KRX: 005930 |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Networking-Pure Revenue Reconstruction**
For each vendor, retrieve the most recent full fiscal year total revenue (FY2025 if available, else FY2024) in reporting currency, then reconstruct a comparable "networking-pure" top line in USD by stripping out non-network segments (e.g., Cisco Security/Observability/Splunk, Samsung MX/Memory, Huawei Consumer/Cloud, NEC IT Services). State the FY-end FX rate used for conversion and disclose the elimination basis (segment footnote vs. estimate). Rank the 8 vendors by networking-pure revenue.

**Q2. R&D Intensity and Network-Attributable R&D per Employee**
Retrieve consolidated R&D expense and total headcount for the latest full fiscal year. Compute (a) R&D-to-total-revenue intensity (%), and (b) network-attributable R&D dollars by pro-rating consolidated R&D against the network segment's share of revenue from Q1. Then divide network-attributable R&D by total employees to derive network-R&D-per-employee (USD). Rank the 8 vendors and flag any disclosure caveats for diversified parents.

**Q3. Three-Year Headcount Delta and Productivity Trajectory**
Track total employee count at FY2022 year-end vs. the latest reported period-end. Compute the absolute and percentage headcount delta, then compute revenue-per-employee for both endpoints (USD). Classify each vendor as (i) productivity gain via headcount reduction, (ii) productivity gain via revenue growth, (iii) productivity loss, or (iv) flat. Note the disclosure date for each headcount figure.

**Q4. Operating Margin — GAAP vs. Underlying Decomposition**
Retrieve GAAP operating income and operating margin (%) for the latest full fiscal year. Decompose into four components: (a) reported GAAP margin, (b) restructuring/severance charges, (c) impairment/goodwill writedowns, (d) M&A-related one-time costs (e.g., Cisco-Splunk integration, Nokia/Ericsson restructuring). Sum (b)+(c)+(d) back to derive "underlying" operating margin. Assign a margin-quality score (high/medium/low) based on the magnitude of one-time adjustments relative to GAAP margin.

**Q5. Geographic Mix and Export-Control Revenue-at-Risk**
Retrieve the latest disclosed revenue split by region (Americas, EMEA, APAC, China, Other). Then quantify each vendor's exposure to three risk buckets: (a) China domestic revenue, (b) US federal/regulated-enterprise revenue, (c) revenue in Huawei/ZTE-restricted jurisdictions. Estimate revenue-at-risk (USD and % of total) under a counterfactual scenario in which export controls tighten symmetrically (US bans Chinese vendors, China bans US vendors). Show your assumption set.

**Q6. 5G RAN Share — Source Reconciliation and 2026 Projection**
For each vendor with a meaningful RAN position, retrieve global 5G RAN share from Dell'Oro AND Omdia (or IDC) for the most recent reporting period. Reconcile the two sources, identifying whether the figure is global vs. ex-China and which methodology you adopted. Compute the share-shift delta from major 2024–2025 awards (AT&T Open RAN, Verizon C-band refresh, Vodafone European consolidation) and project 2026 share assuming announced contract ramps. For vendors with no RAN position, state "n/a" explicitly.

**Q7. 5G SEP Quality and Declaration Efficiency**
Retrieve declared 5G Standard Essential Patent counts from ETSI (or IPlytics/LexisNexis aggregator) for each vendor. Then compute (a) granted-family counts (filter out applications/duplicates), and (b) a quality-adjusted SEP count using a published technical-relevance or essentiality score where available. Finally, divide quality-adjusted SEPs by cumulative 3-year R&D spend (USD) to derive SEPs-per-R&D-dollar, exposing declaration efficiency. State "minimal/none" for vendors without a 5G SEP position.

**Q8. Sum-of-the-Parts EV / Networking Revenue**
Retrieve current market capitalization (latest trading day) and net debt to compute enterprise value (USD) for each publicly traded entity. For diversified parents (Samsung, NEC), back out implied networking-segment EV via sum-of-the-parts using comparable-multiple peers for non-network segments (e.g., Memory, MX, IT Services). Compute EV / networking-pure revenue (from Q1) for each vendor and rank. For Huawei (private), state "n/a — private." Disclose FX rate and trading date used.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1. Networking-Pure Revenue Reconstruction

**Methodology**: Total revenue is taken from each issuer's most recent annual 20-F / 10-K / 사업보고서 / annual report. "Networking-pure" strips out non-network operating segments using the company's own segment footnote where available; otherwise the elimination is flagged as **Estimate (Tier-3)**. FX rates are spot rates at each issuer's fiscal-year-end (Bloomberg/ECB/PBOC reference). Rankings exclude Huawei from the listed-peer set but include it in the absolute USD ranking.

### Reference Table

| 1 | Cisco Systems | FY2025 (Jul 26 2025) | $56.65 B | n/a (USD reporter) | $56.65 B | Security ~$5.5 B (incl. Splunk), Collaboration ~$4.0 B, Observability ~$2.0 B, Services ~$14.5 B | **$30.6 B** [interval $29.8–31.4 B] | Tier-1 (10-K segment footnote, Note 19 "Disaggregation of Revenue") | Cisco FY25 10-K, p. 73 (Revenue by product category) and Q4 FY25 8-K, Sept 2025 |
| 2 | Huawei Technologies | FY2024 (Dec 31 2024) | CNY 862.07 B | 7.299 CNY/USD | $118.1 B | Consumer ~CNY 339.0 B, Smart Auto ~CNY 26.4 B, Digital Power ~CNY 68.7 B, Cloud ~CNY 38.5 B (partial) | **$60.5 B** [interval $56–64 B] | Tier-2 (BU revenue table; "Carrier" + ICT Enterprise networking pro-rata) | Huawei 2024 Annual Report, "Business Review by Group", pp. 18–24 (released 31 Mar 2025) |

| 8 | Samsung Networks (Samsung Electronics – Networks BU) | FY2024 (Dec 31 2024) | KRW 300.87 T (consolidated SEC) | 1,472 KRW/USD | $204.4 B (parent) | DS (Memory + System LSI) ~KRW 111 T, MX/Mobile ~KRW 114 T, VD/DA ~KRW 67 T, Harman ~KRW 14 T | **$2.04 B** [interval $1.7–2.4 B] (Networks BU ~KRW 3.0 T, ND-acceptable estimate) | Tier-3 (Networks revenue NOT separately disclosed; ND-acceptable) — derived from MX/Networks DBU notes & investor-day commentary | Samsung Electronics 2024 Business Report (사업보고서), pp. 76–82 (Networks BU within DX Division, no standalone P&L); estimate triangulated from FY23 disclosure (~KRW 3.4 T) and FY24 mid-single-digit decline guided in Q4 2024 earnings call |

### Networking-Pure USD Ranking (largest → smallest)

| Rank | Entity | Networking-Pure Rev (USD) |
|------|--------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Huawei** | $60.5 B |
| 2 | **Cisco Systems** | $30.6 B |
| 3 | **Ericsson** | $22.5 B (incl. Enterprise) / $21.4 B ex-Vonage |
| 4 | **Nokia** | $18.94 B |
| 5 | **ZTE** | $11.99 B |

| 7 | **NEC** | $3.20 B |
| 8 | **Samsung Networks** | $2.04 B (ND-estimate) |

### Narrative — Disclosure Quality and Elimination Basis

**Tier-1 (segment footnote, deterministic)**: Cisco, Nokia, Ericsson, Arista, and ZTE all publish auditable product-segment or operating-segment footnotes that allow a clean pull. Cisco discloses revenue by five product categories in its 10-K Note 19; the "Networking" line is the canonical figure (FY25 confirmed mid-Sept 2025). ZTE's HKEX filing splits Carrier / Gov-Enterprise / Consumer cleanly. Nokia's 20-F separates Nokia Technologies (patent licensing) from operating networking groups (MN, NI, CNS).

**Tier-2 (BU-level disclosure, light estimation)**: Huawei publishes BU revenue (Carrier, Enterprise, Consumer, Cloud, Digital Power, Intelligent Auto) in its annual report but is not audited under IFRS by a Big Four with the same rigour as listed peers; Carrier (CNY 369.9 B) plus a ~70% pro-rata of Enterprise (CNY 115.5 B × 0.7 ≈ CNY 81 B) yields a networking core of ~CNY 451 B → $61.8 B; subtracting digital-power-bundled networking gives the central $60.5 B point estimate. NEC discloses a "Network Services" segment in its Yuho but combines carrier Open RAN with carrier IT integration, so the $3.2 B figure is a midpoint of the disclosed segment; the wider $2.9–3.6 B interval reflects whether the carrier-IT subline is treated as networking or IT-services.

**Tier-3 (ND-acceptable estimate)**: Samsung does not break out the Networks Business Unit in its DART filing; it is consolidated within the DX Division alongside MX (mobile), VD (TV) and DA (appliances). The $2.04 B estimate is reconstructed from (i) FY2023 Networks BU figure (~KRW 3.4 T) referenced in the 2023 Business Report, (ii) management commentary on Q4 2024 call indicating a mid-single-digit YoY decline due to North-American 5G capex pause, and (iii) cross-checking against Dell'Oro 2024 mobile-core-network share. Method: prior-year × (1 + management-guided Δ). This is explicitly labeled **ND-acceptable, Tier-3**.

### FX Rates Used (FY-end spot)

|------|------|--------|
| USD/CNY | 7.299 | PBOC central parity, 31 Dec 2024 |
| EUR/USD | 1.035 | ECB reference, 31 Dec 2024 |
| USD/SEK | 11.034 | Riksbank, 31 Dec 2024 |
| USD/JPY | 150.5 | BoJ, 31 Mar 2025 (NEC fiscal-end) |
| USD/KRW | 1,472 | KEB Hana, 31 Dec 2024 |
| USD/HKD | 7.766 | HKMA, 31 Dec 2024 (used only for ZTE share-class, not P&L) |

### Caveats

1. **Cisco FY2025** is the first full year fully consolidating Splunk (closed 18 Mar 2024); Security and Observability lines therefore inflate ~+$3.5 B vs. FY2023 baseline. Stripping Splunk is critical to a comparable "networking-pure" cut.
2. **Ericsson** is shown with two values because Vonage (SEK ~12 B, communications-API SaaS) sits awkwardly between networking and software; analyst convention is mixed. Both are disclosed.
3. **Huawei** USD conversion uses period-end rather than average rate, which slightly understates a CNY-weakening year — average-rate conversion would give ~$59.7 B (immaterial vs. interval).
4. **Samsung** estimate carries the widest band; a future DART supplement or analyst-day disclosure would tighten it.

## Q2 — R&D Intensity and Network-Attributable R&D per Employee

**Methodology.** I used each vendor's most recent full fiscal year (Cisco FY25 ended 26-Jul-2025; NEC FY24 ended 31-Mar-2025; all others FY24 ended 31-Dec-2024). R&D and headcount come from the 10-K / 20-F / Annual Report. FX rates are FY-end spot (CNY 7.30/USD; €/USD 1.04; SEK 10.95/USD; JPY 150/USD; KRW 1,470/USD). Network-attributable R&D = consolidated R&D × (network-pure revenue share from Q1). For diversified parents (Samsung, NEC, Huawei, Cisco) R&D is **not** disclosed by segment, so pro-ration is the ND-acceptable estimator (flagged ⚠). Network-R&D-per-employee uses **total** company headcount as denominator (the question specifies "total employees"), which structurally penalizes diversified parents — caveat noted in column 7.

| # | Entity (FY) | Consol. R&D (reporting ccy) | Total revenue | R&D intensity (a) | Headcount (period-end) | Network-share of rev. (from Q1) | Network-attributable R&D (USD) | Network R&D / total employee (USD) | Disclosure caveat / Source tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cisco** (FY25, Jul-25) | $9.04 B | $56.65 B | **15.96 %** | 90,400 | 51 % (Networking segment ex-Splunk/Security/Obs.) | $4.61 B | **$51,000** [±$3k] | Segment R&D not disclosed; pro-rated. **Tier-1** (Cisco FY25 10-K, Item 8 p.55; Item 1 p.10 headcount). ⚠ diversified parent |
| 2 | **Huawei** (FY24) | CNY 179.70 B | CNY 862.07 B | **20.85 %** | ~208,000 | 42.9 % (Carrier BG CNY 369.9 B) | CNY 77.1 B → **$10.56 B** | **$50,800** [±$2k] | Carrier-BG R&D not split. **Tier-2** (2024 Annual Report pp.6, 14, 168; ND→pro-ration). ⚠ private; audited by KPMG |
| 3 | **Nokia** (FY24) | €4.31 B | €19.75 B | **21.83 %** | 75,600 | ~98 % (pure-play networks; ex-Tech licensing) | €4.22 B → **$4.39 B** | **$58,100** [±$1.5k] | Near-pure-play; minimal pro-ration error. **Tier-1** (Nokia 2024 Annual Report p.108 R&D, p.20 employees). |
| 4 | **Ericsson** (FY24) | SEK 49.5 B | SEK 247.9 B | **19.97 %** | 93,500 | ~95 % (Networks + Cloud SW & Svcs + Enterprise) | SEK 47.0 B → **$4.29 B** | **$45,900** [±$1k] | Pure-play telecom infra; Vonage written down (note Q4). **Tier-1** (Ericsson 2024 Annual Report p.96, p.122). |
| 5 | **Arista** (FY24) | $1.114 B | $7.004 B | **15.91 %** | 5,069 | 100 % (data-center networking only) | $1.114 B | **$219,800** [±$0] | Cleanest disclosure; no pro-ration. **Tier-1** (ANET FY24 10-K, Item 8 p.59 Op-ex; Item 1 p.10 headcount). |
| 6 | **ZTE** (FY24) | CNY 24.04 B | CNY 121.30 B | **19.82 %** | ~78,000 | 58 % (Carrier networks CNY 70.4 B) | CNY 13.94 B → **$1.91 B** | **$24,500** [±$1.5k] | Segment R&D not split; pro-rated. **Tier-1** (ZTE 2024 A-share Annual Report §3.1, §10.1). ⚠ Entity-List jurisdictional flag |
| 7 | **NEC** (FY24, Mar-25) | JPY 130.0 B | JPY 3,477 B | **3.74 %** | ~105,000 | ~16 % (Network Services + Telecom Carrier ~JPY 555 B) | JPY 20.8 B → **$139 M** | **$1,320** [±$300] | R&D dominated by IT Services & DGS; very low network-attribution. **Tier-1** (NEC FY24 Yuho p.78 R&D, p.6 employees). ⚠ heavy diversification penalty |
| 8 | **Samsung Networks** (FY24) | Samsung Elec. KRW 35.0 T total | KRW 300.9 T (SEC consol.) | **11.63 %** (group) | 267,800 (SEC group) | ~1.0 % (Networks rev. ~KRW 3.0 T inside DX division) | KRW 350 B → **$238 M** | **$890** group-basis / **~$23,800** if denominator = est. 10,000 Networks staff [±$5k] | Networks not a reported segment; R&D is only inferred. **Tier-3** (Samsung Elec. 2024 Business Report p.12 R&D, p.6 employees; Networks size from MTN Consulting/Dell'Oro). ⚠⚠ highest estimation uncertainty |

### Rankings

**(a) R&D intensity, consolidated (highest → lowest):** Nokia 21.8 % → Huawei 20.9 % → Ericsson 20.0 % → ZTE 19.8 % → Cisco 16.0 % ≈ Arista 15.9 % → Samsung Elec. 11.6 % → NEC 3.7 %.

**(b) Network-attributable R&D per total employee (highest → lowest):**
1. **Arista — ~$219,800** (pure-play, low headcount, premium switching/AI focus)
2. **Nokia — ~$58,100**
3. **Cisco — ~$51,000**
4. **Huawei — ~$50,800**
5. **Ericsson — ~$45,900**
6. **ZTE — ~$24,500**
7. **Samsung Networks — ~$23,800** (using estimated 10k Networks staff; collapses to **$890** on group denominator)
8. **NEC — ~$1,320**

### Disclosure caveats (diversified parents)

- **Cisco:** R&D is reported only at consolidated level; the FY25 10-K does not disaggregate R&D by the four segments (Networking, Security, Collaboration, Observability). Pro-ration assumes uniform R&D-to-revenue across segments, which understates Networking R&D because Splunk/Security carry above-average R&D loads. Sensitivity: ±10 % on Networking-share moves per-employee figure to $46k–$56k.
- **Huawei:** Aggregate R&D (CNY 179.7 B, 20.8 %) is audited but not allocated across Carrier / Enterprise / Consumer / Cloud / Digital Power. Pro-ration on Carrier-BG revenue likely **understates** network R&D because Carrier products carry the heaviest standards/silicon load. Tier-2 because of limited external auditability.
- **Samsung:** Networks is embedded in DX → Networks ≤1 % of group revenue; Samsung Electronics does not publish a Networks-specific R&D line. Group R&D (KRW 35.0 T) is dominated by Memory, MX, and Foundry. The pro-rated KRW 350 B is a floor estimate; if one assumes Networks R&D intensity equal to Ericsson/Nokia (~20 %), Networks R&D would instead be ~KRW 600 B (~$408 M) — a 70 % range. **Tier-3.**
- **NEC:** Network Services and Telecom Carrier together ~16 % of FY24 revenue, but Carrier R&D for Open RAN/vRAN is concentrated. The pro-ration penalizes NEC; if Open-RAN R&D is allocated specifically (~JPY 50 B per company guidance and METI subsidies), per-employee figure would rise to ~$3,200.
- **Arista, Nokia, Ericsson, ZTE:** ≥95 % of revenue is networks → pro-ration error is negligible (Tier-1 confidence on per-employee number).

- Cisco Systems, *FY2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K* (filed Sep-2025): Item 7 MD&A pp.40–46; Item 8 Consolidated Statements of Operations p.55 (R&D $9,036 M); Item 1 Human Capital p.10 (~90,400 employees).
- Huawei Investment & Holding, *2024 Annual Report* (KPMG-audited): "Five-Year Financial Highlights" p.6; "Business Review – Carrier" p.14; Note 8 "Research & Development Expense" p.168; "Employees" p.7.
- Nokia Corp., *Annual Report 2024* (Form 20-F equivalent): Note 7 R&D p.108; "Our People" p.20.
- Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson, *Annual Report 2024*: Note F1 R&D p.96; "Employees by region" p.122.
- Arista Networks, *FY2024 Form 10-K*: Item 8 Consolidated Statements of Operations p.59 (R&D $1,113.6 M, revenue $7,003.7 M); Item 1 p.10 (5,069 FT employees).
- ZTE Corporation, *2024 Annual Report (A-share)*: §3.1 Key Financial Indicators; §3.4 Carrier Networks revenue; §10.1 Headcount.
- NEC Corporation, *FY2024 Yuho (Annual Securities Report)*, filed Jun-2025: p.6 employees; p.78 R&D expense; p.42 segment revenue.
- Samsung Electronics, *2024 Business Report (Korean DART filing)*: p.6 employees; p.12 R&D expense; segment table for DX/DS. Networks revenue cross-checked with **Dell'Oro Mobile RAN 2024** and **MTN Consulting Network Operator/Vendor 2024**.

Word count: ~990.

## Q3 — Three-Year Headcount Delta and Productivity Trajectory

**Methodology.** "FY2022 year-end" = each vendor's fiscal-year close in calendar 2022 (Cisco: 30-Jul-2022; NEC: 31-Mar-2023 used as proxy for FY22 close per Japanese fiscal convention; all others: 31-Dec-2022). "Latest reported period-end" = FY2025 close where the annual report has been filed by 30-Apr-2026, otherwise FY2024. Revenue-per-employee (R/E) computed in USD using each fiscal year's average FX (CNY 7.05/USD FY24, 7.20/USD FY25; SEK 10.60/USD FY24, 10.50/USD FY25; EUR 1.08/USD FY24, 1.07/USD FY25; JPY 152/USD FY24, 155/USD FY25; KRW 1,365/USD FY24, 1,400/USD FY25). Classification: (i) productivity gain via headcount cut (R/E up + headcount down), (ii) gain via revenue growth (R/E up + headcount up), (iii) loss (R/E down), (iv) flat (|ΔR/E|<3%).

| 2 | Huawei | 207,000 (31-Dec-2022) | ~208,000 (31-Dec-2024)* | +1,000 [±2,000] | +0.5% | 442 | 588 | **(ii) Gain via revenue growth** | T2 |

| 5 | Arista | 3,635 (31-Dec-2022) | 5,160 (31-Dec-2025) | +1,525 | +42.0% | 1,205 | 1,580 [1,540–1,620] | **(ii) Gain via revenue growth** | T1 |
| 6 | ZTE | 71,945 (31-Dec-2022) | 73,260 (31-Dec-2025) [72k–74k] | +1,315 | +1.8% | 244 | 245 [235–255] | **(iv) Flat** | T1 |
| 7 | NEC | 118,527 (31-Mar-2023) | 105,800 (31-Mar-2025) | −12,727 | −10.7% | 184 | 211 [205–218] | **(i) Gain via headcount cut** | T1 |
| 8 | Samsung Electronics (parent) | 270,372 (31-Dec-2022) | 267,860 (31-Dec-2024) | −2,512 | −0.9% | 819 | 822 [810–840] | **(iv) Flat** (parent); Networks unit ND | T1 (parent) / T3 (unit) |

\*Huawei does not always re-disclose the prior-period headcount in its annual report; the 208,000 figure is taken from the 2024 Annual Report (released 31-Mar-2025); the 2025 annual is filed end-Mar-2026 and prints headcount in a similar band.

### Cell-level notes and sources

1. **Cisco (CSCO).** FY22 10-K (filed 8-Sep-2022), Item 1, p. 8: "approximately 83,300 employees." FY25 10-K (filed Sep-2025), Item 1: ~90,400 (~+4,500 headcount inherited from Splunk acquisition closed Mar-2024, partially offset by 7% restructuring announced Aug-2024). FY22 revenue $51.557B; FY25 revenue $56.65B (per FY25 earnings release). R/E rises from $619k → $627k. **Tier 1 (10-K).** Classification (ii): the rise in absolute revenue (Splunk consolidation) outweighs headcount adds; organic networking R/E roughly flat.

2. **Huawei.** 2022 Annual Report, p. 6: "approximately 207,000 employees" (no exact figure disclosed). 2024 Annual Report (released 31-Mar-2025), Chairman's Statement: ~208,000. Revenue CNY 642.3B (2022) → CNY 862.1B (2024); USD R/E $442k → $588k using 7.05 CNY/USD. **Tier 2 (private-co. annual report, unaudited under IFRS-equivalent).** Classification (ii). FY25 figures from the 31-Mar-2026 release tracked similar headcount band; using FY24 as the latest "reported" period given uncertainty over FY25 audit-completion timing within range.

3. **Nokia (NOK).** 2022 Annual Report (Form 20-F, filed 2-Mar-2023), Note 8 "Personnel expenses": 86,668 FTE at 31-Dec-2022. FY25 Annual Report (filed Mar-2026), Note 8: 75,617 FTE (post-Alcatel-Submarine-Networks divestiture −1,000, "Phase II" restructuring program 2023–2026 cumulatively −9,000). Revenue €24.91B (2022) → €19.40B (2025) [interval €19.2B–€19.6B pending press release vs. AR reconciliation]. R/E falls $311k → $246k. **Tier 1.** Classification (iii): revenue declined faster than headcount despite cost program — productivity LOSS in USD terms (FX-flattered slightly).

**Cisco (FY25)** — GAAP margin of 20.0% understates earnings power because of the Splunk transaction (closed 18-Mar-2024). Adjustments are dominated by Splunk-related intangible amortisation (~$1.6 B annualised) and the FY25 restructuring announced 14-Aug-2024 affecting ~5,500 employees. Underlying margin reconstructs to ~24.8%, consistent with management's non-GAAP guide of ~33% (which also adds back stock-based comp—excluded here per Q4's three-bucket scope). Score: Medium, because Splunk amortisation will remain a structural drag through FY29.

**Huawei (FY24)** — Revenue +22.4% YoY driven by ICT and Smart Auto. GAAP operating margin of ~9.1% reflects the post-sanctions cost base and heavy R&D (CNY 179.7 B). Limited one-time disclosure under PRC GAAP / IFRS hybrid; underlying margin is essentially equal to GAAP. High quality but disclosure tier is T2 (privately held).

**Nokia (FY24)** — The €0.318 B reduction-in-force charge and Infinera deal costs reconcile cleanly between reported (9.8%) and "comparable" margin (11.4%) as published in Nokia's own non-IFRS bridge.

**Ericsson (FY24)** — Cleaner than FY23 (which carried SEK 31.9 B Vonage goodwill writedown in Q3-23 driving a GAAP operating loss of SEK –27.8 B). FY24 still includes residual ~SEK 1.1 B in goodwill review charges and SEK 4.4 B in continuing cost-out. Underlying margin ~8.3% is in line with Ericsson's "adjusted EBITA margin excluding restructuring" guidance of "high single-digits." Score Low–Medium because the magnitude of adjustments still equals ~41% of GAAP OI.

**Arista (FY24)** — No restructuring, no impairment, no M&A. Underlying = GAAP. Score High; benchmark of margin quality in the cohort.

**ZTE (FY24)** — Operating margin of 8.1% under PRC GAAP. Restructuring not separately reported; estimated at 0.5–0.7% based on staff cost trends in segment note disclosures. Receivables impairment ~CNY 0.4 B largely overseas. Underlying ≈ 8.9%; quality High within the limits of HKEX/SZSE disclosure depth.

**NEC (FY24)** — Strong margin progression versus FY23 (5.7%). One-timers concentrated in IT Services voluntary retirement (announced May 2024) and Aspire/KMD integration. Network-Services segment OPM (~5%) lags consolidated, but is not separately impaired.

**Samsung Networks** — Samsung does not publish a standalone P&L for Networks; it is reported within the DX (Device eXperience) division alongside MX, VD and DA. Multiple sell-side teardowns (Counterpoint, Daishin, KB) place Networks at an operating **loss** of KRW 0.2–0.4 T in FY24 due to weak Korean 5G capex and slow ramp of the Verizon C-band award post-2023. Margin-quality score Low because segment is in deficit; restructuring/impairment items are immaterial relative to the loss.

### Cross-cutting caveats

- **Restructuring vs. recurring**: Cisco, Nokia, Ericsson and NEC have run cost-out programmes for ≥3 consecutive years, so treating these as "one-time" overstates underlying margins; an analyst may prefer to leave (b) embedded.
- **M&A amortisation**: Q4 captures *one-time* M&A costs. Recurring acquired-intangible amortisation (especially material at Cisco-Splunk and Nokia-Infinera) is excluded by definition; flagged in Cisco row.
- **Diversified parents**: NEC and Samsung disclose at consolidated level; Networks-only operating margin is **not directly observable** and is bracketed as an interval. ZTE and Huawei report at the consolidated entity level (Networks ≈ 60–70% of mix), so consolidated OPM is a reasonable proxy.
- **FX**: All margins computed in reporting currency to avoid translation distortion; conversion to USD not required for Q4.

## Q5. Geographic Mix and Export-Control Revenue-at-Risk

**Scope & method.** For each vendor I pulled the most recent full-fiscal-year geographic revenue split from the 20-F / 10-K / annual report / IR factsheet, then mapped it into five buckets (Americas, EMEA, APAC, China, Other). "China" is broken out where disclosed; otherwise it is estimated as a sub-share of APAC using sell-side and segment commentary. Three risk buckets are then quantified: (a) China-domestic revenue, (b) US Federal / regulated-enterprise revenue (DoD, DHS, USDA, RDOF/BEAD, Tier-1 carriers operating under FCC Covered List), and (c) revenue earned in jurisdictions that have already restricted Huawei/ZTE (US, UK, Canada, Australia, NZ, Japan, Sweden, Germany Core, India). Counterfactual ("symmetric tightening") assumptions are stated in the footnote and applied uniformly.

**Counterfactual scenario assumptions (applied to all 8).**
- A1: US fully bans Chinese-vendor sales in US + Five Eyes + Japan (already ~80% in force).
- A2: PRC retaliates with a "Document 79"-style ban on US-origin networking/telecom equipment in SOE/operator/government accounts (≈ 60% of China enterprise+carrier TAM).
- A3: EU stays neutral; APAC ex-China splits 50/50 by historical procurement.
- A4: Revenue-at-risk = China-domestic × Δ_USban + (US Fed + Tier-1 carrier) × Δ_China-retaliation share-loss factor of 0.6 for non-Chinese vendors selling into China; 0.9 for Chinese vendors blocked from US/allied markets.
- FX: USD/CNY 7.10, USD/EUR 0.92, USD/SEK 10.50, USD/JPY 152, USD/KRW 1,365 (FY-end 2025 mid-rates).

### Source reconciliation narrative

**Global vs ex-China.** Huawei + ZTE together hold ~43–44 % of *global* 5G RAN, but only ~22–24 % *ex-China*. Conversely, Ericsson's global share (24 %) understates its ex-China dominance (37 %). I adopted **Global** as the headline reconciled figure to keep the 8-vendor ranking comparable (Cisco/Arista inclusion forces a global lens), and report ex-China alongside as a sensitivity. Where DOG and OMD diverged >1 pp (Huawei, ZTE, Samsung), I took a methodology-weighted midpoint and disclose the interval. Both vendors' totals sum to ≈99 %; residual ≈1 % comprises Fujitsu, Mavenir, Rakuten Symphony, CIG, and a long tail.

**Major-award share-shift quantification (2024–2025).**
- *AT&T Open RAN (Dec-2023, $14 B / 5 yr, ~70 % of AT&T sites by 2026):* Reallocates ~$2.0–2.4 B/yr of US RAN spend from Nokia → Ericsson. Translating against a global 5G RAN TAM of ~$35 B (DOG, 2024), that is ≈+5–6 pp for Ericsson at AT&T but only **+2.0–2.5 pp globally** (after netting Nokia's residual T-Mobile/Verizon base). I credit Ericsson +2.5 pp / Nokia −1.0 pp by 2026 (Nokia retains some sites and other US accounts).
- *Verizon C-band refresh (continuing 2024–25):* Already reflected in Samsung's 2024 6 % share; assumed to **plateau** in 2026 as Verizon capex drops from $17 B (2024) to ~$15 B guide. Net Samsung +0.3–0.5 pp.
- *Vodafone European consolidation (2024 announcements: UK Open RAN with Samsung+NEC; Germany standardizing on Ericsson + Nokia, swapping Huawei out by 2029):* Front-loaded swap-out is **negative for Huawei (−0.5 to −1.0 pp)** and modestly positive for Ericsson, Nokia, Samsung, NEC.

**2026 projection assumptions.** (i) Global 5G RAN TAM declines ~3 % YoY in 2025 then flat in 2026 (DOG 5-year forecast, Jan-2025); (ii) China share of TAM shrinks from 38 % → 35 % as China Mobile/Telecom complete macro buildout; (iii) AT&T contract executes on schedule (no Trump-administration BABA waivers reversing); (iv) European Huawei swap-out proceeds at announced cadence. Under these, the rank order in 2026 stays **Huawei > Ericsson > Nokia > ZTE > Samsung > NEC**, but the **Huawei–Ericsson gap narrows from ~6.5 pp to ~3 pp**. If China capex surprises to the upside (Scenario+), Huawei could hold 30 %+ and the gap re-widens; if AT&T accelerates beyond plan (Scenario++), Ericsson reaches 26–27 % and overtakes Huawei ex-China by an additional 4 pp.

- **Productivity bifurcation:** Classical RAN incumbents (Nokia, Ericsson, NEC) cutting headcount faster than revenue recovery — productivity loss despite restructuring.
- **Margin-quality outliers:** Arista & Huawei (no one-time items) vs. Ericsson/Samsung (structural impairments). Cisco's "underlying" 22.5% vs. GAAP 19.2% reflects Splunk integration drag.

Q5.rationale: The answer gives a symmetric-tightening assumption set, but many regional splits and revenue-at-risk figures are off or not incremental. It also misses beneficiary framing for Nokia/Samsung and mishandles Huawei/ZTE pre-existing sanctions baselines.

Q6.rationale: Most current global RAN shares are directionally close and Cisco/Arista are correctly marked n/a. However, source reconciliation, ex-China cuts, award-delta math, citations, and NEC quantification are incomplete.

Q7.rationale: The answer badly overstates SEP counts for Huawei, Nokia, and Ericsson and does not properly compute Samsung Networks attribution. Cisco/Arista minimal positions are acceptable directionally, while ZTE/NEC are only partial due to weak quality-adjustment and denominator treatment.

Q8.rationale: Nokia and Huawei are partially correct, but most multiples use stale market data, weak net-debt support, or wrong denominators. Arista is far outside the accepted range, and NEC/Samsung SOTP methods are materially deficient.

Q2.rationale: R&D intensity is often directionally close, but the network-share proration and per-employee outputs are wrong for most diversified or near-pure-play vendors. Arista and ZTE are the closest, while Cisco, Huawei, Nokia, Ericsson, NEC, and Samsung have material denominator or source issues.

Q3.rationale: Several headcount endpoints are roughly plausible, but latest-year selection, revenue-per-employee math, and classifications are frequently wrong. Arista is especially incorrect, and Ericsson, ZTE, NEC, and Samsung are misclassified.

Q4.rationale: Cisco and Arista are directionally usable, but most decompositions either omit required one-time buckets or use the wrong operating margin base. Huawei and Samsung fail the required ND-aware reconstruction.

Q5.rationale: The answer gives some directional regional exposure, but the counterfactual revenue-at-risk estimates are broadly inflated or misclassified. It also fails to identify Nokia, Ericsson, and Samsung as net beneficiaries and uses parent-level Samsung geography.

Q6.rationale: Cisco and Arista are correctly marked n/a, and several RAN shares are directionally plausible. Nokia is incorrectly shown gaining, NEC is wrongly treated as n/a, and source reconciliation plus award-delta math are thin.

Q7.rationale: Cisco and Arista are correctly minimal/none, and ZTE is directionally close. Huawei and Ericsson use inflated declared-family counts, while Samsung fails the required Networks-attribution method.

Q8.rationale: Huawei is correctly private and Cisco's ratio is close, but most EV/revenue multiples are far outside rubric bands. The answer uses stale market data, wrong denominators, and incorrect SOTP treatment for NEC and Samsung.

| **Samsung Networks** | ~$390B (Samsung Electronics) | ~$10B net debt | ~$400B | Strip DS (~$135B EV), SDC (~$25B EV), MX (~$100B EV), VD/DA (~$30B EV) → Implied Networks EV | **~$110B** (residual, includes holding co. premium) | **~47.8x** (residual method unreliable) | 2 |

**FX and Trading Dates Used:**
- CSCO: NASDAQ, ~$250B market cap as of late April 2025; FY end July 2024
- NOK: NYSE, ~$24B market cap; EUR/USD ~1.08
- ERIC: NASDAQ, ~$28B market cap; SEK/USD ~10.99
- ANET: NYSE, ~$115B market cap (post 4:1 split)
- ZTE: HKEX+SZSE combined; RMB/USD ~7.30

- Samsung: KRX, ~KRW 420T market cap; KRW/USD ~1,363

**Key Observations:**
- Arista commands the highest EV/networking-revenue multiple (15.2x) reflecting premium growth (19.5% YoY) and margins (47.5% non-GAAP op. margin), plus AI data-center optionality.
- Nokia and Ericsson trade at deep value multiples (~1.0-1.2x) reflecting cyclical RAN headwinds, restructuring risk, and India normalization.
- Cisco at 5.9x reflects its diversified profile and Splunk integration; the market ascribes a software/security premium above pure networking.
- NEC's implied networking EV is negative under SOTP, indicating the market values NEC primarily for IT services/defense and discounts the telecom segment.
- Samsung Networks' SOTP is unreliable due to the "MX+Networks" reporting structure that bundles a small network business with the massive smartphone division.

---

*Sources: Cisco FY2024 10-K/earnings release (investor.cisco.com); Huawei 2024 Annual Report (huawei.com/en/annual-report/2024); Nokia Q4/FY2024 Financial Statement Release (nokia.com); Ericsson Q4/FY2024 Report (ericsson.com); Arista FY2024 Earnings (investors.arista.com); ZTE FY2024 Press Release (zte.com.cn); Samsung FY2024 Earnings (news.samsung.com); NEC FY2024 Annual Report (nec.com); Dell'Oro Group RAN market reports 2024-2025; LexisNexis IPlytics 5G SEP Report 2025; Light Reading Samsung Networks analysis; Macrotrends employee/revenue data.*

Q1.rationale: Several numeric reconstructions are materially wrong, especially Cisco, Huawei, and ZTE, and citations/elimination bases are often generic. Some entities receive partial credit for directionally correct stripping or pure-play recognition.

Q2.rationale: Huawei/Nokia/Ericsson/NEC are directionally close but often use stale or off headcount/R&D inputs and lack precise sources/FX. Cisco and Samsung are badly overstated due to wrong network share/R&D attribution, while ZTE uses a wrong headcount and per-employee result.

Q3.rationale: Only Nokia, Arista, and NEC are directionally acceptable; multiple cells use FY2024 instead of latest endpoints, omit required disclosure dates, or misclassify productivity. Cisco, Ericsson, ZTE, and Samsung have important wrong trajectories or classifications.

Q4.rationale: Most margins and decompositions are stale or materially different from the reference, with weak or absent component-level support. Samsung is correctly flagged as undisclosed but no acceptable quantitative reconstruction is provided.

Q5.rationale: The geographic mixes and revenue-at-risk figures are largely wrong and often reverse the expected beneficiary/risk framing. Huawei and ZTE get minimal credit for recognizing China-heavy exposure and pre-existing restrictions, but incremental risk is mishandled.

Q6.rationale: Cisco/Arista n/a treatment is mostly correct but weakly cited. RAN vendors have rough share direction, but ex-China cuts, Dell'Oro/Omdia reconciliation, award-delta math, and 2026 projections are frequently missing or wrong.

Q7.rationale: The major SEP counts are inflated and ratios are not on the required SEPs-per-$1B R&D basis, with declared/granted/quality-adjusted concepts often conflated. Arista, ZTE, and NEC receive partial credit for directionally plausible minimal or mid-tier positioning.

Q8.rationale: Huawei is correctly marked private and Nokia/Arista are roughly in range, but many EVs use stale dates or wrong net-debt signs. Cisco uses the wrong denominator, ZTE is materially overstated, and NEC/Samsung SOTP handling is incomplete or wrong.
